text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Emir met former parliament speakers to discuss formation of new government. The cabinet, in line with the constitution, resigned on Tuesday after the second Kuwaiti parliamentary election since the 1991 Gulf War.
- Kuwait Oil Company says Kuwait and Saudi Arabia celebrated the production of one billion oil barrels from the neutral zone. The two allies share the output from the border zone.
- Emir to ask Crown Prince Sheikh Saad to form new government.

- Some of the newly-elected parliamentarians and a senior government official will meet on Friday to agree on a candidate for the post of parliament speaker, a well-placed source said. The new parliament will hold its first meeting on October 20.
- "I'll enter house with turban," said controversial Moslem Shi'ite scolar Hussein Qalaf. The Iran-educated Qalaf won a parliament seat in Monday's election.
- New cabinet to mirror change in parliament.
- Qalaf calls for Iran role in Gulf security.
